# dsh-agent-checkin
> One plugin, two jobs: run every installed AI client's daily check-in from inside DeepSeek Harness,
and wire those clients' models into DSH — with a loopback-only dashboard.
English | 中文 | Español | Português | हिन्दी
## What it does
This plugin connects the AI clients you already have installed to DeepSeek Harness (DSH) in three wa
s plugin connects the AI clients you already have installed to DeepSeek Harness (DSH) in three ways:

1. **Check-in aggregation** — runs one check-in round across every supported platform, then
reports

each platform's result *and* its live credit balance in a single place.
2. **Local clients as model

providers** — reads the model catalog of the AI clients already signed
in on this machine (TRAE, Qod

er CN, WorkBuddy, Baidu DuMate, WPS Lingxi) and registers them as
providers, so their models appear

in the model picker and can be used in chat.
3. **Model wiring** — takes an OpenAI-compatible or Ant

hropic-compatible endpoint and registers
it as a provider route inside DSH.

All three read from the same set of local clients. The balances in the dashboard and the models
in t
he picker belong to the same accounts.

The **token usage panel** is a fourth, independent surface: it reads DSH's own session logs and
repo

rts how many tokens each provider and model has consumed, and at the bottom gives a **model
leaderbo

ard with task recommendations** (capability scores from a public board; "which models exist"
from th

is machine only). It touches none of the above — see
The token usage panel.

## Usage
### Checking in
| Surface | How |

| Command | `/checkin` — one round across all platforms |
| Command | `/checkin trae,lingxi` — only

the listed platforms |
| Command | `/checkin --force` — ignore the same-day idempotency guard and cl

aim again |
| Command | `/checkin-status` — show the previous round without re-running |
| Tool | `c

heckin_run` — the same thing, callable by the agent |
| Settings panel | the "Run check-in now" butt

on — one click runs a round and shows per-platform results |
| HTTP | `GET /dsh-agent-checkin/status

` — JSON snapshot for a dashboard |

**Nothing is claimed by default.** The plugin ships with `allowClaim: false`, which forces every
run

into read-only mode. A check-in that actually changes an account balance is a real-world
action, so
it must be switched on deliberately:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

You can also flip it from the host's **plugin settings panel** — `allowClaim`, `pythonCommand`,
`hom

eDir`, `timeoutMs` and `pushResult` are hot-reloadable, so a change takes effect on the very
next ru
n without restarting the host.

The claiming switch in that panel is genuinely wired up: it writes the new value back to your
profil

e's `cordis.patch.yml` through the host `configEditor` service (file lock, validation, atomic
write,

rollback on failure), and the volatile hot-commit described above makes the running instance
read t

he new value immediately. One click is enough — no hand-editing YAML, no restart. If the write
fails

the panel shows the server's real reason rather than a fake success, and if the value was
already w
hat you asked for it says so instead of claiming it saved something.
### The dashboard
Open `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dsh-agent-checkin` in a browser on the same machine. It is served only

on
the loopback interface: any request whose `Host` or `Origin` is not a loopback address gets a 40

3,
so another local app (or a page reached through DNS rebinding) cannot read your balances.
The page follows the same honesty rules as the command output:

- **Read-only is stated up front.** With `allowClaim: false` the top of the page says the round
clai

med nothing.
- **Read-only platforms are a separate section.** Platforms with no claim endpoint are

never
counted as "check-in succeeded", because there was no such action.
- **There is no cross-platf

orm total.** Points, credits and 灵感值 are different currencies; adding
them produces a number that me

ans nothing. The page says so instead of showing one.
- **Unknown balances show `—`, not `0`.** Zero

is a reading; "could not read it" is not.
- **What was read gets shown.** Each platform keeps its u

sable balance under a different field name
(TRAE and WorkBuddy CN under `total_credits`).
Normalisat

ion lives in the engine's `bridge.py`; the plugin repeats it defensively, so balances
still render i

f you point `homeDir` at your own copy of the engine without that patch.
